comment: Every rule here exists because a real bug or a real review finding produced it. When a human catches a new error category, it becomes a rule here so a machine catches it next time.

rules.description: The gateway must sign with EdDSA, never the shared-key HMAC path
rules.why: Under HS256 every verifier can also mint; the gateway must use mint_eddsa so verification and minting authority stay separate.
rules.fix: In continuity/gateway.py replace mint(... key=state.key ...) with mint_eddsa(... secret=state.signing_secret ...).

rules.description: Device keys are never stored in plaintext
rules.what: state.py stores a plaintext device key attribute
rules.why: A stolen state snapshot would hand over usable device keys, defeating the hardware binding on token minting.
rules.fix: Store only hash_secret(self.salt, device_key) in Session.device_hash and compare with safe_eq.

rules.what: gateway.py binds to a wildcard address
rules.why: This service is a local fallback issuer. Exposed on a network it becomes an authentication bypass for anyone who can reach it.

rules.what: a non-standard HTTP client was imported
rules.why: The fallback path must run on a machine that may have no package index reachable — during an outage, precisely.
rules.fix: Use urllib.request (stdlib) and confine it to health.py.

rules.description: Network egress confined to the health probe
rules.why: The only sanctioned egress is the identity-plane probe. Anything else is an unreviewed path out of the process.
rules.fix: Move the call into health.py, or remove it. The gateway itself must never contact a tenant.

rules.why: alg=none is the classic JWT authentication bypass; no code path may ever emit it.
rules.fix: Remove it. Verifiers already refuse anything that is not RS256/EdDSA/HS256 as appropriate.
